extras.document_section: S3-compatible object storage below the big three
extras.verified_at_basis: checked against the live service on 2026-11-11
extras.quota_verbatim: EUR 3.95 per TB, prepaid, up to 100 TB per account, 30 million objects per bucket
extras.limits_verbatim: `request-rate`/ratio cap: egress beyond the 10:1 allowance has no published price — unverified. Prepaid billing only. Endpoint not published on the page; s3.datalix.de does not resolve (DNS NXDOMAIN), so the endpoint must be taken from the customer panel.
extras.egress_verbatim: Verbatim: "Ingress ist kostenlos und unbegrenzt. Egress enthaelt 10 TB pro 1 TB Storage." — i.e. an included ratio of 10 TB egress per 1 TB booked storage, not truly unmetered. At 20 TB booked that is 200 TB/month included, which covers the 30 TB/month serving load with 6x headroom.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Direct S3 origin; put Cloudflare in front to make even the included 200 TB/month irrelevant.
extras.tooling_verbatim: Any S3 SDK / rclone / AWS CLI (vendor states full S3 compatibility)
extras.interface_verbatim: S3 API, IAM-enabled, multi-redundant in Frankfurt
extras.price_verbatim: $4.44/TB at 5 TB (EUR 19.75 = $22.19) and $4.44/TB at 20 TB (EUR 79.00 = $88.75). Cheapest true S3 object storage in this survey.
extras.agent_focus: Cheap-paid lane: S3-compatible object storage outside AWS/Azure/GCP/Alibaba/Cloudflare/B2/IDrive-e2. Target = true $/TB/month floor with free-or-generous egress, computed at the 5 TB and 20 TB tiers. EUR->USD at 1.1234 (frankfurter.app, 2026-10-21).

binding_note: the 100 TB per account cap ends the booking; up to 30 million objects fit in one bucket, and no per-object size cap is stated
